record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the IOI manual circuit using optimal ablation and compares circuit and component loss measurements across ablation methods, but does not reproduce the original head-role patching analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI circuit and single-component ablation outcomes. Its comparisons of circuit-search algorithms are not evidence that the resulting circuits have the same head classes or roles as the original; no head-class overlap or role tests are reported. The IOI prompt variants are not evaluated separately.
record.test_reason: The study re-evaluates the Wang et al. manual IOI circuit in GPT-2 small under a new ablation method (optimal ablation) and under mean, resample and counterfactual ablation. It compares the circuit's KL loss gap with Pareto-optimal circuits of similar size. These results bear on V1 (does the manual circuit capture the behaviour) and V5 (does the evaluation depend on the ablation choice). It does not reproduce the head-class or path-patching analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that optimal ablation isolates information deletion from 'spoofing', making it a better measure of component importance and of circuits. On IOI it shows the manual circuit to be approximately optimal for its size. They argue the much higher losses under mean, resample and CF ablation reflect spoofing inflation rather than a flaw in the manual circuit.
record.recipe_differences: Uses optimal ablation and circuit-loss comparisons, alongside zero, mean, resample, and counterfactual ablations; it does not reproduce the original head-class role tests or criteria-based circuit validation.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI loss-gap measurements vary across ablation methods; the reported difference is substantial for circuit evaluation and also appears in aggregate single-component comparisons.
record.problems: The IOI circuit comparisons report relative loss gaps rather than absolute values in the cited text; uncertainty estimates for these IOI results are not stated. The study does not test prompt-variant robustness or the original circuit's head roles.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: UGS-versus-ACDC and other circuit-search algorithm comparisons in Section 3.2 and Appendix F, because they report search performance rather than whether the original head classes or roles are recovered. Greater-Than, factual-recall, and latent-prediction results do not test the IOI claim.

untested.parts: The 26-head / 7-class composition, the head roles, and the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests as defined by Wang et al.
Backup name-mover takeover after ablating name movers.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse of components across tasks.
Whether ACDC, EAP, HCGS or UGS recover the same heads or roles as the manual circuit. Only loss-versus-size Pareto frontiers are reported.
Sensitivity to the prompt distribution. The text notes IOI templates hurt resample ablation, but this is not tested separately.
Name orders, templates and more names are not evaluated separately.

missing.what: Absolute ∆ (KL) of the manual IOI circuit under each ablation method, and its edge count in the paper's graph representation
Mean single-component ∆ per ablation method (zero 0.0584, mean 0.0405, resample 0.0559, CF-mean 0.0412, OA 0.0035, CF 0.0296)

record.verdict_notes: The graph representation (residual rewrite with separate Q/K/V edges, 32,491 edges) differs from Wang et al.'s, so manual-circuit edge counts are not directly comparable. The authors' reading of r3 is that prior ablations inflate ∆, not that the circuit is incomplete. The V1 limits_scope label reflects the numbers, not the authors' interpretation. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates the IOI manual circuit's loss under ablation, but does not test the 26-head, 7-class composition, the stated roles under patching, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria as a set.
Backup-head takeover after ablating main name-mover heads is not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and component reuse across tasks are not tested for the claimed IOI mechanism.
The study compares ablation metrics and circuit-search algorithms, but does not test whether other methods recover essentially the same circuit or components.
The paper compares ablation metrics for IOI circuit evaluation; it does not separately test prompt-distribution variation.
No separate comparison of circuit behavior across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names is reported.
